topic: ND filter maths: each stop halves the light, 10 stops = 1/1024, so 1/60 s becomes ~17 s (simulated sea at 1/60 s vs 17 s)
lines: This glass blocks almost all light.
Each stop halves the light. Ten halvings makes one thousand twenty-four.
Each stop halves the light. Ten halvings makes 1,024.
Your sensor gets a one thousand twenty-fourth of the light, so you need an exposure one thousand twenty-four times longer.
Your sensor gets a 1,024th of the light, so you need an exposure 1,024 times longer.
One sixtieth of a second becomes about seventeen seconds.
1/60 of a second becomes about 17 seconds.
Same waves. At one sixtieth, they're frozen. At seventeen seconds, they're silk.
Same waves. At 1/60, they're frozen. At 17 seconds, they're silk.
The rock doesn't move, so it stays sharp. Only the water blurs.
Three stops, eight times longer. Six stops, sixty-four times.
Block the light, buy yourself time.

youtube.title: This Glass Blocks 99.9% of Light. Here's Why. (ND Filter Maths)
youtube.description:
A 10-stop ND filter (ND1000) halves the light ten times: 2^10 = 1,024, so only ~0.1% reaches the sensor. To keep the same exposure, the shutter must stay open 1,024× longer: 1/60 s becomes ~17 s (1/60 × 1,024 ≈ 17.07 s). 3 stops = 8× longer, 6 stops = 64×. The sea frames are a simulation: one instant vs an average over 17 s of moving waves, with a static rock.
